# Implementation Ecosystem

Covers library support, language runtime availability, HSM readiness, cloud
provider status, and browser adoption. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for
full source details.

## Cryptographic Libraries

| Library | PQC Status | Key Details |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| **OpenSSL 3.5** | ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA | Released April 8, 2025. LTS until April 8, 2030. Default TLS keyshares include X25519MLKEM768. Handshake time 13ms → 15.5ms with hybrid [21][42] |
| **AWS-LC** | ML-KEM, ML-DSA | First open-source module with ML-KEM in FIPS 140-3 validation (certificates #4631, #4759, #4816). CRYSTALS-Kyber support ending across AWS endpoints in 2026 |
| **BoringSSL** | ML-KEM | Chrome's TLS backend. ML-KEM implemented following September 2024 standardization |
| **Bouncy Castle** | ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA | Java 1.79 (December 2024). TLS ML-KEM cipher suites in Java 1.81 [36] |
| **wolfSSL** | ML-KEM, ML-DSA, LMS, XMSS | Version 5.8.4 (early 2026). FIPS 140-3 with PQC in development |
| **SymCrypt** | ML-KEM, ML-DSA | ML-KEM November 2024, ML-DSA December 2024. Windows Server 2025, Windows 11, SymCrypt-OpenSSL 1.9.0 for Linux [44] |
| **liboqs** | ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, HQC, Falcon | Version 0.15.0 (November 2025). SPHINCS+ removal planned in 0.16.0. CVE-2025-52473 for HQC |
| **rustls** | ML-KEM (hybrid) | X25519+ML-KEM in rustls 0.23.22+. ~1,600 additional handshake bytes, 80-150 μs overhead |

## Language Runtimes

### Go

Go 1.24 (February 2025) enabled X25519MLKEM768 by default when
`Config.CurvePreferences` is nil [22][43]. This is the most aggressive default
PQC adoption among language runtimes. Removed X25519Kyber768Draft00 from Go 1.23.
Kubernetes v1.33 (April 2025) inherited PQC support automatically [22].

### Java

- JDK 24: ML-KEM KEM API via JEP 496 with ML-KEM-512/768/1024
- JDK 27: Hybrid key exchange for TLS 1.3 via JEP 527
  (X25519MLKEM768, SecP256r1MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024)
- ML-DSA JAR signing planned for JDK 26 (March 2026)

### Python

Fragmented landscape — no single authoritative library:
- **pqcrypto:** Precompiled bindings (January 2026 release)
- **liboqs-python:** Wrapper for liboqs C library
- **quantcrypt:** Uses PQClean binaries
- **python-cryptography:** No PQC roadmap found in this research

### Rust

rustls provides ML-KEM via `prefer-post-quantum` feature flag. ~1,600 additional
handshake bytes, 80-150 microseconds overhead.

## Hardware Security Modules

| Vendor | Product | PQC Status |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| **Thales** | Luna HSM v7.9 | Native ML-KEM and ML-DSA (June 2025). FIPS 140-3 Level 3 in progress [37] |
| **Entrust** | nShield fw v13.8.0 | NIST CAVP validated (September 2025). ML-DSA-44/65/87, ML-KEM-512/768/1024 [38] |
| **Crypto4A** | QxHSM | Quantum-safe architecture from ground up. FPGA-based for algorithm agility. FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated, 140-3 submitted |
| **Utimaco** | Se-Series | Quantum Protect package. ML-KEM, ML-DSA, LMS, XMSS. CAVP testing passed mid-2025 |

CAVP certification achieved rapidly — multiple vendors validated within months
of FIPS publication (August 2024). PKCS#11 v3.2 (standardizing ML-KEM for HSMs)
still in development.

## Cloud Providers

| Provider | PQC Status |
|----------|-----------|
| **AWS** | ML-KEM hybrid PQC TLS in KMS, ACM, Secrets Manager. AWS-LC first FIPS-validated open-source module with ML-KEM. Kyber support ending 2026 |
| **Google Cloud** | PQC KEMs in Cloud KMS preview. Full availability expected 2026 |
| **Microsoft Azure** | General PQC roadmap: early adoption 2029, completion 2033. Quantum-resistant symmetric keys via Managed HSM. No specific ML-KEM timeline found |

### Adoption Statistics (October 2025)

- **50%+** of human-initiated traffic to Cloudflare uses PQ encryption [20]
- **39%** of top 100k domains support PQ key agreement (up from 28% six months
  prior) [20]
- **3.7%** origin server support (up from 0.5% in 2023) [20]
- **0.05%** connection breakage from middlebox/protocol ossification issues [20]
- X25519MLKEM768 transmission: ~3 kB vs 64 bytes for X25519 alone [20]

## Standards Infrastructure

| Standard | PQC Status |
|----------|-----------|
| **IETF TLS** | draft-ietf-tls-ecdhe-mlkem-04 in RFC Editor Queue [15] |
| **IETF IKEv2** | RFC 9370 published May 2023, up to 7 additional key exchanges [16] |
| **PKCS#11** | v3.1 standardizes LMS/HSS; v3.2 will add ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, ML-KEM (in development) |
| **NIST CAVP** | ML-KEM and ML-DSA validation enabled August 2024 |
| **FIPS 140-3** | AWS-LC first module with ML-KEM validated |

## Gaps and Limitations

- Python PQC landscape is fragmented with no clear consolidation path; the
  widely-used python-cryptography library has no public PQC roadmap
- Azure Key Vault specific ML-KEM timeline not found; only general Microsoft
  roadmap (2029/2033)
- PKCS#11 v3.2 finalization date unknown — over 18 months after FIPS publication,
  potentially fragmenting HSM vendor implementations
- mbedTLS (ARM) has no official ML-KEM support; developers waiting for NIST
  standardization
- Safari PQC lag until October 2025 is significant given Apple's mobile market
  share
- HSM vendor claims are from their own announcements; independent verification
  of FIPS 140-3 validation status not confirmed for all vendors
- Origin server PQC adoption (3.7%) substantially lags browser support,
  indicating server-side infrastructure is the bottleneck
